title: Hemodialysis
what: A machine cleans your blood when your kidneys cannot. Blood passes through a filter and returns to your body.
why: For severe kidney failure - usually ongoing, several times a week.
duration: one session usually takes about 4 hours, usually 3 times a week
tell_doctor: All your medicines - some are given after the session
How you felt after the last session
If your weight has changed, or you have swelling or shortness of breath
If your fistula hurts, is swollen or has lost its "buzz"

prepare.title: Weight
prepare.text: Weigh yourself every day. Between sessions, watch how much you drink.

prepare.title: Drinking and eating
prepare.text: Your doctor will set limits on water, salt, potassium and phosphorus. Do not change them on your own.

prepare.title: Fistula
prepare.text: On the arm with the fistula: no tight clothes, watches, blood pressure cuffs or needle sticks. Check the buzz and thrill every day.

bring: Notes of your weight and blood pressure
A blanket, a book or headphones
steps: You are weighed and your blood pressure is measured
The nurse cleans your arm and places two needles in the fistula, or connects to a catheter
Blood goes into the machine, is cleaned and returns to you
You lie or sit for several hours
The nurse watches your blood pressure and how you feel
At the end the needles are removed and the spots are pressed
feel: A needle prick in the fistula
During the session you may get cramps, weakness or dizziness - tell the nurse
after: Press on the needle spots until they stop bleeding
Get up slowly - you may feel dizzy
Follow your diet and the limit on water
red_flags: Bleeding from the fistula that does not stop - press on it and call your local emergency number
Severe shortness of breath or chest pain - call your local emergency number
The fistula has stopped buzzing and thrilling - call the dialysis unit right away
Fever, chills, or redness at the access site

faq.a: No. Skipping is dangerous: potassium and fluid build up in the blood. If something stops you, call the unit right away.
Yes, if you arrange dialysis in the other city in advance. Talk about it with the unit.

reminders.text: Dialysis tomorrow. Weigh yourself in the morning, and take your list of medicines and a blanket.
